question.text: Young's modules of material of a wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> and cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Y</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the length of the wire is doubled and cross-sectional area is halved then Young's modules will be:

solution.text: Young’s modulus depends on the material not length and cross-sectional area. So Young’s modulus will remain same irrespective of the dimension of the wire.
